title: TAT-3763 — Perps available-to-trade percentage is a clean rounded number on initial load
description: Opens the live Perps order-entry form and proves the balance-percent pill renders a whole, unclipped percentage on initial load (AC1), then drives the slider through trusted UI input to prove the already-working interaction path still renders a whole, unclipped percentage (AC2). Data prerequisites, enforced by the gate-cdp and setup-unlock nodes: the Extension runtime must be reachable over CDP on the configured port, and the fixture wallet's active account must have a non-zero Perps tradeable balance — a zero balance makes the default balancePercent 0 and leaves AC1 unobservable.

setup-status.intent: Resolve the Extension checkout and adapter status before proving the fix

gate-cdp.intent: Fail fast unless the Extension CDP runtime is reachable

setup-unlock.intent: Ensure the wallet is unlocked before opening the Perps order form

setup-open-home.intent: Leave any previous Perps route so the order form mounts fresh and the initial-load state is genuine

setup-open-order-entry.intent: Open the ETH Perps order-entry form where the available-to-trade percentage pill renders

ac1-wait-percent-pill.intent: AC1: confirm the balance-percent pill is visible on initial load before asserting and capturing it

ac1-probe-initial-load.intent: AC1: read the initial-load percentage value and its clipping geometry without mutating any state

ac1-assert-percent-is-whole-number.intent: AC1: the initial-load percentage is a clean rounded whole number, not a long decimal

ac1-assert-percent-not-clipped.intent: AC1: the pill's text fits its field, so the user never sees the reported truncated value

ac1-assert-slider-on-step-grid.intent: AC1: the slider's aria-valuenow sits on its declared step=1 grid instead of an off-step decimal

ac1-clear-capture-orphans.intent: AC1: clear wedged capture-helper sessions so the screenshot comes from capture-helper, not the raster fallback

ac1-screenshot-initial-load-percent.label: AC1: initial load shows a clean rounded percentage in the pill, not a truncated decimal
ac1-screenshot-initial-load-percent.intent: AC1: capture the visible pill on initial load, the exact surface the ticket reports as truncated

ac2-press-slider.intent: AC2: move the slider through a real click, as the ticket's reproduction step 5 describes

ac2-key-increment-1.intent: AC2: nudge the focused slider with trusted keyboard input to a non-zero percentage

ac2-key-increment-2.intent: AC2: continue moving the slider through trusted keyboard input

ac2-key-increment-3.intent: AC2: settle the slider on a non-zero percentage so the assertion is not trivially satisfied by 0

ac2-wait-percent-pill.intent: AC2: confirm the three trusted key presses actually moved the slider to 3 before asserting

ac2-probe-after-interaction.intent: AC2: read the post-interaction percentage value and its clipping geometry

ac2-assert-percent-value.intent: AC2: the pill reflects the exact percentage the user's slider interaction produced

ac2-assert-percent-is-whole-number.intent: AC2: the already-working interaction path still renders a whole number after the fix

ac2-assert-percent-not-clipped.intent: AC2: the post-interaction pill still fits its field, confirming no regression

ac2-clear-capture-orphans.intent: AC2: clear wedged capture-helper sessions before the second capture

ac2-screenshot-after-interaction.label: AC2: after moving the slider the pill shows 3, a whole unclipped percentage
ac2-screenshot-after-interaction.intent: AC2: capture the moved-slider state so reviewers can see the interaction path is unchanged
